content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** Section 22.4 fails the ASSIGN fallback on a material term. M&I may "freely assign" in any merger, reorganization or sale of assets/stock/securities, while Tri City's consent-free carve-out is confined to a merger where the survivor becomes an Affiliate of a financial institution with at least $100,000,000 of capital and surplus — so an acquisition or asset sale to any other successor would need M&I's consent. No written-notice mechanic exists for either party's successor assignment.

**Cure (fallback level, single surgical replace in p0289):** broadened Customer's carve-out to "a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Customer's assets, stock or securities", added "in each case upon written notice to the other party" covering both carve-outs, and deleted "freely" from M&I's right. The consent requirement and "not be unreasonably withheld" standard were already met and were left verbatim; the Section 21.11 proviso and M&I's own successor language were preserved.

Noted in the rationale rather than flagged: Section 21.11.B obliges M&I to continue Services after a Customer Change in Control (no Vendor termination right, though it caps volume at prior period plus 25%), and Section 11.3 is redacted but appears to be a Customer termination right per the Section 11.1 fee carve-out.
